lines: …You’re real.
I heard boots on the line and told myself it was the pipes again.

choices.label: I thought I was the last one.

lines: So did I. For eleven years.
I’m Mara. There were six of us out here once.
Mara. I keep this outpost. Kept it, anyway.
And you came down my line from the old shelter. I thought that place was empty.

choices.label: It is now. My father died.

lines: …I’m sorry. Then it’s just us, as far as either of us knows.
Up. They took the lift up looking for the surface and the cage came back empty.
I stayed with the beds.
The pressure valve blew a week back. The pump’s been knocking dry ever since, and the intake’s choked with silt.
No water means no lift: I won’t run that drive dry.

choices.label: I could help with the water.
What would the lift cost me?

lines: Here’s how it’d go.
You bring up the valve from the sump and clear the intake. I fit the valve and get the pump running. In return, {liftReward}.
And the water stays here. The beds die without it.

choices.label: Deal.
choices.detail: You: valve from the sump, clear the intake · Mara: fits the valve, then {liftReward} · The outpost keeps its water

lines: Parts. {price}. Bring them to the cage and I’ll free the drive.
My pump stays dry, but that’s my problem, not yours.

choices.label: Deal.
choices.detail: You pay {price} · Mara repairs the lift · Her tap stays dry

lines: The old maintenance chimney, back along the line. Twenty feet, rungs long gone.
Two good ropes and something to anchor them. {chimneyCost}. Nobody owes anybody.

choices.label: I’ll find my own way up.

lines: Valve’s down in the sump, by the intake. Mind the cold.
Water first. Then I keep my end.
Bring the parts to the cage. I start when they’re all there.
{status}
Grow beds, a pump, a lift. The crews built it as a waystation between the shelters and the transit level.
When the tunnels came down it was just the six of us and the beds.
My tap’s dry again and the line valve’s turned toward your place. I can see it from here.
We all need it. That’s why we made a deal.
I watched you take my spare valve off that shelf.
Put it back, or bring me another.

choices.label: Here. It’s yours.
choices.locked: You don’t have a valve on you.

lines: My spare valve’s gone from the shelf.
I’m not saying it was you. I’m saying it’s gone.

choices.label: I took it. Here.
choices.locked: You don’t have a valve on you.

lines: …Thank you.
